title: Nicholas Throckmorton to Elizabeth I, Paris, 10 July 1559, in his Cipher 1: BL Add MS 4136 f. 32 (DECODE R2988)

documents.shelfmark: BL Add MS 4136 f. 32 (old 9), main text (DECODE R2988)

plaintext.source: not in Forbes or CSP Foreign (only the 8 July despatches are calendared)

transcription.source: DECODE image IMG_R2988_I20714_P.jpg, lines re-cut at measured line centres
transcription.notes: Counted by script from the first-pass sign lines L01-L15 of main_decrypt.txt (separators and struck signs dropped); line 16 not transcribed. NOTES give ~550 signs for lines 5-15.

system.summary: Throckmorton's Cipher 1: a letter alphabet of digits, letters and invented signs with homophones, nulls and dotted code signs for words and names.

diacritics.note: a dot over a sign marks a code word

system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's Cipher 1 key image for Throckmorton's correspondence, attached to DECODE R2988
system.notes: Corrections to the key: x and upsilon = i; y = f/h; z = m; rho = d/t; long-s t and flat-topped 6 = w; Q = be; xi and dotted q = your Majesty; zeta and doubled signs = nulls; K = all (?).

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo identifies the cipher as his Cipher 1 and attaches the key, but no decipherment of this letter is printed (Forbes, CSP Foreign) or online

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Tomokiyo unsolved.htm and project throckmorton notes: f. 32 carries Throckmorton's own letter of 10 July 1559 in his Cipher 1, for which Tomokiyo gives the key; no printed decipherment.
Subagent decryption of R2988 main text with Tomokiyo Cipher 1 key; crops misaligned, lines 1-5 only.
Main text re-cut at measured line centres; lines 1-4 read securely, lines 5-15 decode to English with key corrections (x,υ=i; z=m; ∫t=w; Q=be).

Pass 3 over lines 5-15 (main_decrypt.txt): flat-topped 6 = w, q = u, zeta = null inside words, dotted q = your Majesty, K = all(?); lines 5-15 read at about 85% (about 470 of 550 signs); twelve code signs open.
CSP Foreign vol. 1 pp. 362-369 (BHO) and Forbes I: only the 8 July 1559 despatches are calendared; no text of the 10 July letter.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from wod1568, which had joined three systems on BL Add MS 4136 ff. 32-33: Throckmorton's Cipher 1 letter of 10 July 1559 (throck1559), the f. 32 marginal word-sign code (throck1559margin) and John Wood's 1568 line (wod1568). This profile keeps Throckmorton's 10 July 1559 letter in Cipher 1 (R2988 main text) only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): R2988 linked to main_decrypt.txt (sign transcription with passes 1-3 interlined); the key corrections and additions copied verbatim from NOTES.md and main_decrypt.txt to texts/key.md (the base Tomokiyo key is an image on DECODE). Line 16 was never transcribed

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): main_decrypt.txt and the running reading R2988.txt read through; lines 1-5 build one sentence, from line 6 there are [...] holes every few words ('to [...] knowledge of considering the present [...] to dispatch [...] gentleman'; 22 of 60 sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py). R2988 relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved; fraction_read 0.85 -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b36): DECODE R2988 refetched (image 3269 x 4205 and Tomokiyo's key image); neighbours R2986 (f. 30, to Cecil 9 July), R2987 (f. 31, to the Council 9 July), R2990 (ff. 34-35, to Cecil 13 July) fetched and opened: sibling letters in the same Cipher 1, no decipherment or copy of f. 32. Forbes I re-checked: no text of the 10 July letter.
Line centres measured by projection (15 lines); lines 5-15 re-transcribed sign by sign at 2-3x (texts/R2988_signs.tsv), look-alike choices marked.

Tomokiyo's key image read in full, including its code list: as G/б, have б̄, had r̄, whom ṭ, upon ḟ, so g̲, this б̲, all K, at O, be Q, in ἰ, your Majesty ξ (also ζ, formerly a null). Decoder research/reading_audit/b36_throck.py.
Code values from sense: q̄ hath (3 contexts; Tomokiyo 'both' fits none), ō good (4), ġ letters (2), π̄ God, ῡ his, ϱ̲ time, V I (one each). Open: 1̲ k̲, ť, r̲ (key 'then' does not fit), v̲, ℓ̄.

Partial reading written (texts/R2988_reading.md, _en.md), aligned word by word with the decoder output. b17 0.35 plain, 0.60 explicit holes (English 1559); look-alike share 30/496 = 0.060 > 0.03 with no confirming text: kept decoded, not read.

outcome.method_basis: Throckmorton's 10 July 1559 letter was deciphered with Tomokiyo's Cipher 1 key image for Throckmorton's correspondence, with seven values corrected; lines 1-4 secure, lines 5-15 about 85%.
outcome.fraction_read_source: 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: only documents that build sentences count; the one letter (729 tokens) is decoded, not read (only its first sentence, lines 1-5, reads whole), so 0. The earlier 0.85 (lines 1-4 secure, ~470 of 550 signs in lines 5-15 given a value, estimated) is withdrawn as a reading figure.
outcome.notes: Unpublished letter: Throckmorton sends a gentleman to report the French King's state, asks credit and reward for him, signs off at Paris the tenth of July. The starred note keyed to line 13 is in the margin word code (throck1559margin). Split 14 Oct 2026 from wod1568. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: relabelled decoded, not read. 23 Oct 2026 (re-read b36): lines 5-15 re-transcribed and decoded with the key's code list; partial reading texts/R2988_reading.md (b17 0.35 plain / 0.60 explicit holes); kept decoded, not read on the look-alike share (6%).

texts.label: R2988, Add MS 4136 f. 32, Throckmorton to Elizabeth I, Paris, 10 July 1559
texts.summary: Throckmorton sends a gentleman, the bearer, to report the French King's state by word of mouth after his two despatches of 8 July (by Gray and, at midnight, by Carew); he asks the Queen to give the bearer credit, praises his diverse and sundry service and asks that it be rewarded. An unpublished letter, not in Forbes or CSP Foreign.
texts.note: Re-read b36 (23 Oct 2026): lines 5-15 re-transcribed sign by sign at full size (texts/R2988_signs.tsv) and decoded with Tomokiyo's Cipher 1 including its code list, which the September passes had not used (have, had, as, so, whom, upon, this, your Majesty ...); the letter now builds into sentences (texts/R2988_reading.md, partial reading; b17 0.35 plain, 0.60 explicit holes). Kept decoded, not read: 30 of 496 letters (6%) rest on look-alike choices (rho t/d, 7 r/g, mu h/b, x i/y, o/a), above 3%, and no contemporary or printed text of the letter exists to confirm them; codes 1k (l. 6), t-dot, r-underline, v-underline, l-bar and two sign groups open. Next: the sibling letters in the same cipher (R2986, R2987 of 9 July, R2990 of 13 July) against Forbes I pp. 157-160, to test whether rho serves for both d and t and to confirm q-bar hath, o-bar good.
